result: The authors identified nine type II neuroblast lineages per hemisphere in the Tribolium embryo, compared to eight in Drosophila and grasshopper. This represents a novel finding showing that the number of type II neuroblasts is not fixed across insects.
evaluation: All reviewers explicitly affirm this finding. The editor states the authors 'present convincing data which confirm the presence of type II NB lineages in beetle...differing in lineage size and number.' Reviewer 1 acknowledges 'they have identified that there are 9 type II neuroblasts in the brain hemisphere during embryonic development.' Reviewer 2 confirms 'there are 9 instead of 8 embryonic type-II NB lineages per brain hemisphere.' Reviewer 3 notes 'identification of an extra neuroblast' as a strength.

result: The authors found that embryonic type II neuroblast lineages in Tribolium are significantly larger than in Drosophila, containing more progenitor cells (average 18.4 at NS13, 16.8 at NS14) and significantly more mature intermediate progenitors.
evaluation: Reviewers consistently accept this finding. The editor notes the data show lineages 'differing in lineage size and number.' Reviewer 1 states 'the lineage size of the type II neuroblasts in the beetle is larger than that in the fly.' Reviewer 2 confirms 'the lineages contain more progenitor cells compared to the Drosophila lineages.' Reviewer 3 acknowledges 'the beetle type II neuroblasts lineages are likely longer than the equivalent ones in Drosophila.'

result: The authors created a Tc-fez/erm enhancer trap line using CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing, with the reporter construct inserted 160 bp upstream of the fez/erm transcription start site. The fez-mm-eGFP co-localized with most Tc-fez/erm-expressing cells in protocerebral structures.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly praise this methodological contribution. Reviewer 1 states 'The authors established a useful enhancer trap line to visualize type II neuroblasts in Tribolium embryos.' Reviewer 2 notes 'The authors generate a fluorescent enhancer trap line called fez/earmuff which prominently labels the mushroom bodies but also the intermediate progenitors (INPs) of the type-II NB lineages.' No concerns are raised about the construct or its validation.

result: The authors demonstrated that type II neuroblast lineages in Tribolium show a largely conserved molecular code compared to Drosophila, with similar expression dynamics of markers (Tc-pnt, Tc-dpn, Tc-ase, Tc-fez/erm, Tc-pros) differentiating type II NBs, intermediate progenitors of distinct maturation stages, and GMCs.
evaluation: All reviewers affirm the conservation of molecular markers. The editor states the data 'confirm the presence of type II NB lineages in beetle with the same molecular characteristics as the Drosophila counterparts.' Reviewer 1 notes 'several genetic markers are also expressed in the type II neuroblasts and their lineages as observed in Drosophila.' Reviewer 2 confirms 'the cell type composition and embryonic development of the type-II NB lineages are similar to their counterparts in Drosophila melanogaster.' Reviewer 3 highlights 'Identification of a conserved molecular signature of type-II neuroblasts between beetles and flies' as a strength.

result: The authors showed that type II neuroblast lineages produce central complex cells, with skh-positive cells located distally to the lineages and some cells co-expressing both Tc-fez/erm and skh markers. Both anterior-median and posterior groups contribute to central complex neuropile.
evaluation: Reviewers accept this finding without challenge. Reviewer 2 states 'the expression of the Cx marker skh in the distal part of most of the lineages provide further evidence that the identified NB lineages are equivalent to the Drosophila lineages that establish the central complex.' Reviewer 3 notes 'some lineaging looking into co-expression of progenitor (fez) and neuronal (skh) markers' as a strength. No concerns are raised about this result.

result: The authors found that Tc-otd is specifically absent from all type II neuroblasts and intermediate progenitors, suggesting its inhibition is required for the development of all these lineages.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge this finding as part of the divergent marker expression patterns. Reviewer 3 notes 'the expression of some of the lineage markers (otd, six3, and six4) is slightly different' as a strength, indicating acceptance of the otd absence data. No reviewer challenges this specific finding, and it is presented as part of the comprehensive marker analysis that reviewers praise.

result: The authors demonstrated that Tc-six3 marks only an anterior subset of type II neuroblast lineages (lineages 1-4 of the anterior-medial group), including both the type II NBs and the fez-mm-eGFP marked INPs/GMCs.
evaluation: Reviewers accept this as part of the marker characterization. Reviewer 2 states 'the expression of the Drosophila type-II NB lineage markers six3 and six4 in subsets of the Tribolium type-II NB lineages (anterior 1-4 and 1-6 type-II NB lineages)...provide further evidence that the identified NB lineages are equivalent to the Drosophila lineages.' Reviewer 3 acknowledges 'identification of transcription factors expression differences in the neuroblasts' as a strength.

result: The authors found that Tc-six4 specifically marks the territory where anterior-medial type II neuroblasts (clusters 1-6) differentiate, with expression in both type II NBs and INPs at NS13, but only in type II NBs at NS14.
evaluation: Reviewers accept this finding as part of the comprehensive marker analysis. Reviewer 2 explicitly mentions 'the expression of the Drosophila type-II NB lineage markers six3 and six4 in subsets of the Tribolium type-II NB lineages (anterior 1-4 and 1-6 type-II NB lineages)' as evidence supporting the identification. No concerns are raised about the six4 expression data.

result: The authors propose that the higher number and greater lineage size of embryonic type II neuroblasts in Tribolium correlate with the previously described embryonic phase of central complex formation, and that increased type II NB activity may contribute to embryonic development of a functional central body and protocerebral bridge.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge this correlation but note the lack of direct causal evidence. Reviewer 2 states 'While the manuscript clearly shows that type-II NB lineages similar to Drosophila exist in Tribolium, it does not establish a direct link between the characteristics of these lineages and a functional larval Cx in Tribolium.' Reviewer 3 explicitly lists as a weakness: 'The link between size and number of neuroblast lineages and the earlier central complex development in beetles is not examined.' The editor notes the data 'lay the foundation for future analysis' of whether differences can be linked to central complex functionality.

result: The authors found that large Tc-pnt-expressing cells and fez-mm-eGFP-expressing cells are mitotically active, with immature-I and -II INPs not dividing while mature INPs are dividing.
evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge this finding. It is presented as part of the comprehensive characterization of the lineages that reviewers praise. Reviewer 1 notes the authors 'successfully identified 9 of those cells' and characterized their properties. The mitotic activity data supports the identification of these cells as proliferative progenitors, which reviewers accept.

result: The authors assigned the nine type II neuroblast clusters into two groups based on their position: one anterior median group consisting of seven type II NBs and one posterior group consisting of two type II NBs.
evaluation: Reviewers accept this organizational scheme. Reviewer 2 discusses the grouping in detail, noting 'there are 9 instead of 8 embryonic type-II NB lineages per brain hemisphere' and that the study provides evidence for their equivalence to Drosophila lineages. The grouping is not challenged and is used by reviewers in their discussion of the findings.

result: The authors found that cells assigned as type II neuroblasts had significantly larger cell diameters (average 12.98 µm) and nuclear diameters (average 8.73 µm) compared to reference samples.
evaluation: Reviewers accept this as supporting evidence for type II NB identification. Reviewer 1 states 'those cells showed characteristics of type II neuroblasts in terms of genetic codes, cell diameter, and cell lineage.' However, Reviewer 1 also notes 'I still have some concerns about the lack of examination of the expression of NB markers. Without examining the expression of at least one unequivocal neuroblast marker, no one can say confidently that it is a neuroblast. However, it is acknowledged that such a marker is currently not available for Tribolium.' This indicates the size data is accepted but not considered definitive alone.

result: The authors found that lineages of type II NBs 5, 6, and presumably 7 of the anterior cluster and the posterior type II NB lineages express neither Tc-otd nor Tc-six3, questioning the generalized role of these factors in subdividing the protocerebrum.
evaluation: Reviewers accept this finding as part of the marker expression analysis. Reviewer 3 notes 'identification of transcription factors expression differences in the neuroblasts' as a strength. The finding is presented as a novel observation about protocerebral subdivision, and no reviewer challenges this interpretation.
